title: the release gate runs the load-sensitive daemon arms in the shared checkout at their test budgets, so an unchanged tree fails and passes by host load
body:
`bin/devbin build release --patch` gates the cut on `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, run in the shared checkout (`bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release`, about line 575). That run includes the daemon_subscriptions and daemon_watch arms, which wait up to 20 s for an event, polling 500 times at 20 ms. On this host fseventsd sits at about 110 percent CPU as its steady state and the one-minute load is in the twenties at rest, so those arms starve: on the v3.0.3 cut the gate failed twice and passed on the third run with nothing changed in the code. Raised by dc and gtools-vc through vc, 2026-09-14.

A gate that an unchanged tree fails and then passes measures the host, not the release, and every re-run costs the cut several minutes. The same family is already known to red by load and to red at a base commit in a matched control, so a red from these arms at the gate is not evidence against the release.

The question for a ruling: do these arms belong in the release gate at their budgets? The candidates: keep them, but run the gate from a private worktree under an isolated HOME with the live daemon out of the way (which the estate's own rule for suites already asks, since a test run writes the estate it lives in); or give the gate a longer event budget than the arms use in development; or move the load-sensitive family out of the release gate and rely on CI's legs for it.


CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): built to the first candidate. The gate runs in a private worktree at HEAD under an isolated HOME with its own target dir, as the estate's rule for suites already asks (`cargo build -p intentd`, then the suite). When every red is in the load-sensitive daemon family (`daemon_subscriptions`, `daemon_watch::`, `a_source_edit_reaches_the_index_and_costs_canon_nothing`), it reruns `-p intentd` once; any other red aborts. The worktree is removed on every exit. Judged (scratchpad batch/judge-0389.txt): the script's own classifier on synthetic logs gives daemon-family only -> rerun once, mixed -> abort, and the block, extracted by its marker, parses. The rerun's timing under real host load is seen at the next cut.
